overview.heading: How the Photo Trend Maker works
paragraphs: You upload one photo, choose one of 19 looks and pick a size. PiCraft sends the photo and a written description of the look to an AI image model, which redraws the whole picture in that style while keeping the subject recognizable. The result comes back as a JPG at the exact pixel size of the shape you chose.

Each look is a different kind of change. The film and camera looks, such as the [80s flashback](/create/photo-trend-maker/80s-flashback) and the [Y2K digital camera](/create/photo-trend-maker/y2k-digicam), change the clothes, the surroundings and the flaws of the picture. The handmade looks, such as the [claymation world](/create/photo-trend-maker/claymation) and the [felt miniature](/create/photo-trend-maker/felt-miniature), rebuild the scene from physical materials. The seasonal looks, such as the [Halloween costume portrait](/create/photo-trend-maker/halloween-portrait), the [Thanksgiving harvest portrait](/create/photo-trend-maker/thanksgiving-harvest), the [Christmas card portrait](/create/photo-trend-maker/christmas-card), the [snow globe](/create/photo-trend-maker/snow-globe) and the [New Year's Eve party flash](/create/photo-trend-maker/new-years-eve-party), dress the subject for a holiday and rebuild the room around them. The rest turn the photo into a toy, a game screen, a blueprint, a newspaper page or a statue.

The size is chosen before the image is made, not after. A 9:16 image is composed for a tall frame, so the subject is not cut off the way it would be if you cropped a square. Each generation costs one credit and gives a new result, so you can run the same photo through several looks and keep the best one.

whatYouGet.title: A finished JPG at the exact size
whatYouGet.description: 1080×1920 for 9:16, 1000×1500 for 2:3, 1080×1440 for 3:4 or 1080×1080 for 1:1. The image is generated for that shape first and then cut to the exact pixel size.

whatYouGet.title: 19 distinct looks
whatYouGet.description: Camera looks, handmade looks, game, print and art looks, and six holiday looks in one form. The [photo trends category](/categories/photo-trends) shows how they group together.

whatYouGet.title: A subject that stays recognizable
whatYouGet.description: The instructions ask the AI to keep face shape, skin tone, age and hair color, and to keep pets and objects recognizable too.

whatYouGet.title: No prompt to write
whatYouGet.description: Upload, choose and download. The wording behind each look is already written and tested, so you never have to describe grain, lighting or materials yourself.

whatYouGet.title: A page for every look
whatYouGet.description: Each look has its own page with examples, best uses and tips, so you can see what to expect before you spend a credit.

useCases.title: Stories and full-screen vertical posts
useCases.description: Choose 9:16 for stories, reels covers and any post that fills a phone screen. The subject is composed for a tall frame instead of being squeezed in afterwards.

useCases.title: Pinterest boards
useCases.description: Choose 2:3 to match the shape Pinterest recommends for standard Pins. Trend looks group naturally into boards, such as retro portraits, toy versions of your pets or handmade scenes.

useCases.title: Profile pictures and avatars
useCases.description: A [3D toy avatar](/create/photo-trend-maker/toy-avatar) or a [bobblehead](/create/photo-trend-maker/bobblehead) in the square size makes a profile picture that still looks like you without being a plain selfie.

useCases.title: Pet photos and small gifts
useCases.description: A [marble statue](/create/photo-trend-maker/marble-statue) or a felt miniature of a dog or a cat makes a funny card, a mug design or a message for a friend who loves their pet.

useCases.title: Holiday cards and seasonal posts
useCases.description: The [Christmas card portrait](/create/photo-trend-maker/christmas-card), the [vintage Christmas snapshot](/create/photo-trend-maker/vintage-christmas), the [Thanksgiving harvest portrait](/create/photo-trend-maker/thanksgiving-harvest) and the [Halloween costume portrait](/create/photo-trend-maker/halloween-portrait) turn one photo, with or without a pet, into a seasonal picture for a card, a family chat or a holiday Pinterest board.

useCases.title: Invitations and group chats
useCases.description: A [fantasy newspaper](/create/photo-trend-maker/fantasy-newspaper) front page or a [photo booth strip](/create/photo-trend-maker/photo-booth) works as a funny invitation header, a birthday surprise or a gift for a group chat.

tips.title: Start with a sharp, evenly lit photo
tips.description: Window light and daylight work best. Blurry, very dark or heavily filtered photos give the AI little to hold on to, and the result drifts further from the original.

tips.title: Make the face or the pet large
tips.description: Close crops and waist-up shots keep the likeness better than a wide scene where the subject is small. Crop the photo first if you need to.

tips.title: Choose the size first
tips.description: The size changes how the image is composed. Pick 9:16, 2:3, 3:4 or 1:1 before you create instead of cropping a finished image, which can cut off hands or heads.

tips.title: Match the look to the photo
tips.description: Camera looks suit casual, well-lit photos with clothes and a background to restyle. Handmade and toy looks suit close portraits and pets. The blueprint poster suits one clear subject standing alone.

tips.title: Try one photo in three looks
tips.description: Every generation is new, so running the same photo through three different looks is the fastest way to find the one that suits the person or the pet.

tips.title: Read the text before you post
tips.description: Some looks draw short words into the image, such as a date stamp or a headline. AI can misspell them, so proofread and generate again if a letter is wrong.

tips.title: Expect a stylized likeness
tips.description: A bobblehead or a clay figure is supposed to look like a toy, not a passport photo. Judge the result by whether friends would recognize you, not by whether every detail matches.

styleGuide.heading: Choosing a look
styleGuide.intro: Each look changes the materials, the color and the mood of the picture. Use this as a quick guide to which one fits your photo and where you plan to post it.

items.title: 80s Flashback
items.description: Faded warm film, flash glare, period clothes and an orange date stamp. Best for [casual selfies and group photos](/create/photo-trend-maker/80s-flashback).

items.title: 70s Slide Portrait
items.description: Sun-faded color, soft grain and a vignette, like an old family slide. Best for [relaxed, outdoor portraits](/create/photo-trend-maker/70s-slide).

items.title: Y2K Digital Camera
items.description: Harsh flash, slightly blown highlights and early-2000s outfits. Best for [friends, parties and mirror-style snapshots](/create/photo-trend-maker/y2k-digicam).

items.title: Night Out Flash
items.description: Bright on-camera flash against a dim city background. Best for [dressed-up portraits and night-out photos](/create/photo-trend-maker/night-flash).

items.title: Photo Booth Strip
items.description: Black-and-white strips with playful poses and heavy contrast. Best for [couples, friends and funny group photos](/create/photo-trend-maker/photo-booth).

items.title: Claymation World
items.description: Matte modelling clay with fingerprints and tool marks. Best for [portraits, pets and anything with a clear outline](/create/photo-trend-maker/claymation).

items.title: Felt Miniature
items.description: Needle-felted wool figures in a small diorama. Best for [pets, couples and cozy scenes](/create/photo-trend-maker/felt-miniature).

items.title: Bobblehead
items.description: A plastic figure with an oversized head on a black base. Best for [selfies and gifts](/create/photo-trend-maker/bobblehead).

items.title: 3D Toy Avatar
items.description: A glossy designer-toy head with sunglasses against a blue sky. Best for [profile pictures](/create/photo-trend-maker/toy-avatar).

items.title: 16-bit Arcade Fighter
items.description: A pixel-art fighter on a side-view stage with a health bar. Best for [gamers and humorous posts](/create/photo-trend-maker/arcade-16bit).

items.title: Blueprint Poster
items.description: White technical lines on cobalt blue with detail views. Best for [a single clear subject such as a pet or a person](/create/photo-trend-maker/blueprint-poster).

items.title: Fantasy Newspaper
items.description: An engraved portrait on a vintage front page with headlines. Best for [birthday jokes and invitations](/create/photo-trend-maker/fantasy-newspaper).

items.title: Marble Statue
items.description: A neoclassical figure carved in white marble in a museum hall. Best for [dramatic portraits and pets](/create/photo-trend-maker/marble-statue).

items.title: Halloween Costume Portrait
items.description: A generic witch, vampire, skeleton or scarecrow costume among carved pumpkins and fog. Best for [pets and playful portraits](/create/photo-trend-maker/halloween-portrait).

items.title: Thanksgiving Harvest Portrait
items.description: A hand-painted autumn table with candles, pumpkins and knitwear. Best for [couples, families and thank-you pictures](/create/photo-trend-maker/thanksgiving-harvest).

items.title: Christmas Card Portrait
items.description: A warm living room with a tree, lights and a fireplace. Best for [couples, families and pets on a holiday card](/create/photo-trend-maker/christmas-card).

items.title: Vintage Christmas Snapshot
items.description: A flash-lit Christmas morning from the late 1970s or early 1980s, with a tinsel tree and wrapping paper. Best for [relaxed selfies, couples and throwback posts](/create/photo-trend-maker/vintage-christmas).

items.title: Snow Globe
items.description: A small figure of you or your pet inside a glass globe with drifting snow and a tiny village. Best for [pets and clear portraits](/create/photo-trend-maker/snow-globe).

items.title: New Year's Eve Party Flash
items.description: Black and gold party clothes, confetti, sparklers and a mirror ball under bright flash. Best for [selfies, couples and party posts](/create/photo-trend-maker/new-years-eve-party).

checklist.heading: Before you post or share
items: Compare the result with your original. If hair color, age, glasses or skin tone changed in a way you do not like, generate again.
Zoom in on faces, hands and any small accessories. These are the places where AI most often goes wrong.
Read every word the look drew into the image, including date stamps, labels and headlines.
Check that the size matches where you will post it: 9:16 for stories, 2:3 for Pinterest, 3:4 for portrait posts and 1:1 for squares.
Look at the background for personal details such as house numbers, license plates or documents before you post a photo of your home.
Get permission from anyone who can be recognized in the picture before you publish it.
Upload the downloaded JPG itself instead of a screenshot, so the platform does not compress the image twice.

limits: AI likeness is never exact. Small details such as freckles, jewelry or teeth can change, and groups of people drift more than a single face does.
The result is a flat JPG, not layers. To change something, pick the look and size again and generate a new image.
Words drawn into the image, such as a date stamp or newspaper headlines, can be misspelled, so always proofread.
Hands, fingers and small accessories can come out wrong, especially in looks that draw many small figures, such as the photo booth strip.
Wide photos with a tiny subject give weaker results than close portraits, so crop first if the face or pet is small.
The size is fixed before the image is made. Switching from 9:16 to 1:1 means generating a new design, which uses another credit.
